title: MP mid-join catch-up + server speed-up authority + bot personality variants
notes: Three deferred MP follow-ups bundled into a single polish sprint. (a) Mid-session RoundState catch-up — a new client joining mid-match currently sees tally:{0,0,0} until the next round resolves; ship RoundState via the snapshot so clients sync immediately. (b) Server-side speed-up pickup authority — speed-up currently no-ops on the server (applyPickupEffect returns undefined for it). (c) Bot personality variants — the existing server bot is roughly miner-ish; expose hunter / coward / miner like the static-profile bot-ai-system.
Scope: bundle these three small features into one sprint so we close the obvious MP polish gaps before moving on to bigger work. None of them require protocol changes.
Out of scope: full Beacon-World-style reconciliation, server-side bot pickup magnet, server-side personality selector UI.

stories.title: Server ships RoundState in snapshot via mp.round-state entity
stories.summary: Add an `mp.round-state` server-side entity that mirrors the existing `kaboom.round-state` singleton (phase/tally/roundNumber/winnerId). Snapshot ships it like any other server entity. Using a server-namespaced id sidesteps the ws-adapter id-collision guard (the local client owns `kaboom.round-state`).
verification: acceptance: Server snapshot now ships RoundState verbatim under a server-namespaced 'mp.round-state' entity id every tick — phase, tally{player,bot,draws}, roundNumber, optional winnerId. Networked.authority='server' so the client knows it's authoritative. Uses a server-namespaced id so the local client's identically-named kaboom.round-state HUD entity isn't shadowed by ws-adapter's id-collision rejection.
examples/backends/node-world-server/src/world.ts: MP_ROUND_STATE_ENTITY constant + snapshot loop emits mp.round-state with RoundState component
+2 unit tests: snapshot has mp.round-state at boot, reflects tally + winnerId after resolve
All 1393 unit tests pass; typecheck clean

stories.title: Client connected-blast-decoder mirrors mp.round-state into local kaboom.round-state
stories.summary: On the connected profile, the decoder reads the `mp.round-state` entity from the snapshot each frame and copies its RoundState component onto the local `kaboom.round-state` entity. Roundresolved events still fire for the audio sting + UI banner, but the actual scoreboard state syncs every frame so a newly-joined client immediately sees the correct tally instead of waiting for the next round-resolve.
verification: acceptance: connected-blast-decoder reads mp.round-state from the local snapshot each frame and merges its phase/tally/roundNumber/winnerId into the local kaboom.round-state singleton. HUD reads from kaboom.round-state unchanged; the timeLimit + matchPhase + matchTarget fields the local client owns are preserved (merge, not overwrite). A newly-joined client immediately sees the live tally instead of starting at {0,0,0} until the next roundResolved event.
examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/connected-blast-decoder-system.ts: MP_ROUND_STATE_ENTITY constant + per-frame mirror loop in the connected-blast-decoder frameUpdate
Typecheck clean; full unit suite green

stories.title: Server applies speed-up pickup to BomberStats.speed + integrates it in movement
stories.summary: Extend ServerBomberStats with a `speed` field (default = PLAYER_SPEED). applyPickupEffect for 'speed-up' bumps speed by +1 cell/s up to a cap (default 12). Movement integration reads the bomber's BomberStats.speed (fallback to PLAYER_SPEED). Snapshot ships speed when it differs from default. Round-reset clears speed back to default.
verification: acceptance: ServerBomberStats now carries a speed field. applyPickupEffect for 'speed-up' bumps speed by SPEED_UP_STEP=1 capped at MAX_SPEED_CAP=12; first pickup goes from baseline PLAYER_SPEED=3.5 to 4.5. Movement integration reads stats.speed (fallback PLAYER_SPEED) so picked-up bombers actually move faster. Snapshot ships speed only when it differs from the baseline so the wire payload stays minimal. Round-reset clears speed by setting BomberStats to defaults without the field.

examples/backends/node-world-server/src/world.ts: speed field on ServerBomberStats + MAX_SPEED_CAP + SPEED_UP_STEP constants; applyPickupEffect speed-up branch wired; integration loop reads per-bomber speed; snapshot loop emits speed when non-baseline
+3 unit tests: single speed-up bumps to 4.5, stacks cap at 12, alice with speed-up out-walks bravo
63 server-map tests pass; typecheck clean

stories.title: Server bot carries a personality (hunter / coward / miner); env-override + default miner
stories.summary: Add `personality` field to the server-side bot record (default 'miner' — matches today's behaviour). KABOOM_BOT_PERSONALITY env var sets it on world boot. tickBotAi reads the personality + branches per-variant logic (next two stories). 'miner' stays the existing baseline (near-soft-block bias).
verification: acceptance: Server bot now carries a personality (BotPersonality = 'hunter' | 'coward' | 'miner', default 'miner'). ServerWorldOptions.botPersonality + KABOOM_BOT_PERSONALITY env var on the node-world-server entry. tickBotAi delegates bomb-place chance to a personality-aware botBombChance() helper. 'miner' keeps the S121 baseline behaviour (chance 0.15 / 0.5 near-soft) unchanged.
examples/backends/node-world-server/src/world.ts: BotPersonality type + personality field on ServerWorld + botBombChance() switch
examples/backends/node-world-server/src/index.ts: KABOOM_BOT_PERSONALITY env override

stories.title: Coward personality: lower bomb chance, more aggressive flee
stories.summary: Coward bot: bomb-place chance drops to 5% (vs miner 15-50%); flee score weighs distance from ALL dangerous cells (not just bomb origins); never bombs without an explicit safe escape route (at least one cardinal neighbour outside ALL active blast cells AND not a hard-wall).
verification: acceptance: Coward personality: base bomb-place chance drops to BOT_BOMB_CHANCE_COWARD=0.05 (vs miner 0.15-0.5). Plus a hasSafeEscape() guard simulates the bomb the coward is about to place AND checks for at least one cardinal neighbour cell that's NOT a hard-wall AND NOT inside ANY blast cell (existing dangerCells union the simulated bomb's cells). Without an escape, the coward refuses to bomb at all. Net effect: coward bombs rarely + only when geometrically safe.
examples/backends/node-world-server/src/world.ts: BOT_BOMB_CHANCE_COWARD constant + hasSafeEscape() helper + 'coward' branch in botBombChance
+1 unit test asserting coward places ≤3 bombs over 3s window

stories.title: Hunter personality: bombs aggressively when a human player is within range
stories.summary: Hunter bot: bomb-place chance jumps to 60% when any alive human player is within manhattan distance ≤ range+1 from the bot's current cell. Base chance stays at 15% otherwise. Soft-block adjacency still boosts to 50%. Direction-pick stays the same (danger-avoid still wins).
verification: acceptance: Hunter personality: bomb-place chance jumps to BOT_BOMB_CHANCE_HUNTER_TARGETED=0.6 when any alive human player's GridPosition is within manhattan distance ≤ (bot.range + 1) from the bot's current cell. Power-ups widen the hunting radius. When no humans in range, hunter falls back to miner-style behaviour (base or near-soft bias). Direction-pick stays the same (danger-avoid still wins so the hunter doesn't suicide chasing).
examples/backends/node-world-server/src/world.ts: BOT_BOMB_CHANCE_HUNTER_TARGETED + isHumanInRange() helper + 'hunter' branch in botBombChance
+1 unit test asserting hunter bombs when alice walked within range
84 server tests pass; typecheck clean

stories.title: Playwright e2e: new client joining after a round resolves sees the tally
stories.summary: Extend tests/e2e/kaboom-multiplayer-roundtrip.spec.ts: alpha joins, self-kills to resolve a round (tally → {0,1,0}). Then a SECOND tab (gamma) joins. Verify gamma's local kaboom.round-state shows tally.bot=1 within ~1s of join (proves the snapshot mirror works), instead of starting at {0,0,0} until another round resolves.
verification: acceptance: New S122 e2e — alpha joins, walks to (1,1), places a bomb to self-kill, waits for the round to resolve (mp.round-state's tally jumps from {0,0,0} to {0,1,0}). THEN gamma joins as a fresh context. Within 10s of joining, gamma's LOCAL kaboom.round-state shows the same non-zero tally. Proves the snapshot-driven mid-join catch-up actually closes the new-client-sees-stale-tally gap. Passes on both chromium + chromium-preview.
tests/e2e/kaboom-multiplayer-roundtrip.spec.ts: +1 S122 test (~22s per project)
Uses KABOOM_BOT_PERSONALITY=coward to suppress bot-side noise during the alpha-self-kill round (otherwise the bot may bomb alpha first + alter the tally direction)
